message.reasoning_content:
We're in round 3 market. Others have no goods either. We hold presidency, influence 2. Bank 30. Prices at sold_counter=4 → price 7. Buying back to sell later? Round start devalues cash (62%). We have 16.12 cash, others more. Buying goods to sell at higher price later? Price decreases with sales; buying moves counter back. Sell prices start at 12... Buying at 7 to sell later at maybe 12 in round 4? But round 4 cash devalues too. Actually goods aren't devalued, cash is. So converting cash to goods protects against devaluation. Buy 2 units costs 15 alashi? cash goes to 1.12 with 2 goods. Then sell at next market—round 4 devaluation applies to cash only. Sell at 12+? counter moves back 2 → 12? sold_counter 4-2=2 → price 10 each. So 20 alashi revenue for 15 spent, plus avoids devaluation. But then devaluation hits that cash at round 5 anyway.

Alternatively buy 1 at 7, sell later at 12 (counter back to 3 → price 9). 9 for 7, plus hedge. Buy 2: cost 15, sell at 10 each = 20. Marginal but cash devaluation: cash 16→ ~9.9 after deval. Buy 2: goods worth 20 sold in r4 market (before deval? deval happens at start of round 4 before market). Sell in round 4: get 20, then round 5 start devalues to 12.4. Buy 1: cost 7, cash left 9.12; sell r4 at 9 → total 18.12 pre-deval vs 16.12 base... hmm.

Actually simplest: buying 2 gives +5 alashi net and shifts wealth to goods. Take choice 2.
